overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated Shorts reveals that high-stakes, first-person hypothetical space survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme cosmic anomalies dominate view velocity, like ratios, and comments (averaging 700-1,000+ views). Conversely, generic psychology trivia ('fake memories', 'songs stuck in head') and repetitive duplicate uploads of identical concepts heavily underperform (averaging <50 views). Audience retention and engagement thrive on extreme visual peril and mind-bending physics.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Peril / 'What If You Fell Into...' Extreme Space Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes, 2 comments) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) outperformed channel baselines by over 500%.
winning_patterns.action: Use visceral, second-person narrative framing ('What happens to your body if...') focused on extreme cosmic environments and physical transformation.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,030 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) generated the highest organic reach among observational facts.
winning_patterns.action: Pair a counter-intuitive physical law with sensory, cinematic imagery to build immediate cognitive dissonance in the first 2 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' uploaded 3 times averaged under 25 views; 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' dropped from 220 to 34 views on repeat attempts.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce a strict anti-repetition rule; never re-upload recycled scripts, and pivot to novel phenomena instead.

weak_patterns.evidence: Titles like 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) saw near-zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Retire passive psychological trivia unless attached to high-stakes micro-drama or visceral survival contexts.
